The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `./executable` is for

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `./executable`. You are free to use any

- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

## Try it

Try out various languages and styles on the [Chroma Playground](https://swapoff.org/chroma/playground/).

## Command-line Interface

A command-line interface to Chroma is included.

Binaries are available to install from [the releases page](https://github.com/alecthomas/chroma/releases).

### Usage with `less`

The CLI can be used as a preprocessor to colorise output of `less(1)`,
see documentation for the `LESSOPEN` environment variable.

The `--fail` flag can be used to suppress output and return with exit status
1 to facilitate falling back to some other preprocessor in case chroma
does not resolve a specific lexer to use for the given file. For example:

```shell
export LESSOPEN='| p() { chroma --fail "$1" || cat "$1"; }; p "%s"'
```

Replace `cat` with your favourite fallback preprocessor.

When invoked as `.lessfilter`, the `--fail` flag is automatically turned
on under the hood for easy integration with [lesspipe shipping with
Debian and derivatives](https://manpages.debian.org/lesspipe#USER_DEFINED_FILTERS);
for that setup the `chroma` executable can be just symlinked to `~/.lessfilter`.

## Projects using Chroma

* [`moor`](https://github.com/walles/moor) is a full-blown pager that colorizes
  its input using Chroma
* [Hugo](https://gohugo.io/) is a static site generator that [uses Chroma for syntax
  highlighting code examples](https://gohugo.io/content-management/syntax-highlighting/)

import subprocess
def lexer_of(inp, filename=None, isfile=False):
    args=["/workspace/executable","-s","monokai","-f","tokens","--trace"]
    if filename: args.append(f"--filename={filename}")
    if isfile:
        open("/tmp/detect/analyse_input","wb").write(inp)
        args.append("/tmp/detect/analyse_input")
        p=subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, timeout=5)
    else:
        p=subprocess.run(args, input=inp, capture_output=True, timeout=5)
    import json
    lines=p.stderr.decode(errors='replace').splitlines()
    name=None
    if lines:
        try: name=json.loads(lines[0]).get("lexer")
        except: name=lines[0][:100]
    return name, p.returncode, p.stderr[:200]
for inp in [b"x\n", b"#!/bin/bash\n", b"\n#!/bin/bash\n", b" #!/bin/bash\n", b"#!/bin/bash", b"#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho\n", b"#!/bin/sh\n", b"#!/bin/ksh\n", b"#!/bin/zsh\n", b"#!/bin/python\n", b"func _ready():\n", b"extends Node\n", b"var x\n", b"#include <foo>\n", b" #include <foo>\n", b"\n#include <foo>\n", b"#ifdef FOO\n", b"#ifndef FOO\n", b"#include <vector>\n", b"using namespace std;\n", b'#include <vector>\nusing namespace x;\n', b"**free\n", b"ctl-opt x;\n", b"dcl-s x;\n", b"*in01\n", b"package main\n", b"package \n", b"export var x\n"]:
    print(inp[:50], lexer_of(inp))
# large content offsets
for n in [0,10,100,500,1000,5000]:
    inp=b"x"*n+b"\nfunc _ready()\n"
    print("offset gd",n, lexer_of(inp)[0])
    inp=b"x"*n+b"\n#include <foo>\n"
    print("offset c",n, lexer_of(inp)[0])
    inp=b"x"*n+b"\n#!/bin/bash\n"
    print("offsetbash",n, lexer_of(inp)[0])
# file vs stdin analyse diff for same
for inp in [b"func _ready()\n",b"#!/bin/bash\necho\n",b"#include <foo>\n",b"package main\n"]:
    print("filevsstdin", inp, lexer_of(inp)[0], lexer_of(inp, isfile=True)[0])
# filename matching precedence over content: filename x.py but bash content
print(lexer_of(b"#!/bin/bash\necho\n", filename="x.py"))
print(lexer_of(b"#!/bin/bash\necho\n", filename="x.unknown"))
print(lexer_of(b"#!/bin/bash\necho\n", filename="python")) # filename as lexer name?
print(lexer_of(b"x\n", filename="python"))
print(lexer_of(b"x\n", filename="text/x-python"))

import glob,re,collections
orders=[]
classmap={}
for f in glob.glob("/tmp/styles_css/*.css"):
    seq=[]
    for line in open(f):
        m=re.match(r"/\* (\w+) \*/",line)
        if m:
            seq.append(m.group(1))
        m2=re.match(r"/\* (\w+) \*/ \.chroma \.([\w-]+)",line)
        if m2: classmap[m2.group(1)]=m2.group(2)
        m3=re.match(r"/\* Background \*/ \.bg",line)
        if m3: classmap["Background"]="bg"
        m4=re.match(r"/\* PreWrapper \*/ \.chroma",line)
        if m4: classmap["PreWrapper"]="chroma"
    orders.append(seq)
# merge: sort tokens by average rank? Check pairwise consistency
tokens=set()
for s in orders: tokens.update(s)
# topological using precedence counts: repeatedly pick token with no predecessors in any seq among remaining
remaining=list(tokens)
merged=[]
while remaining:
    cand=None
    for t in remaining:
        # t can be next if in every seq, all tokens before t are already merged
        ok=True
        for s in orders:
            if t in s:
                idx=s.index(t)
                if any(x in remaining and x!=t for x in s[:idx]):
                    ok=False; break
        if ok:
            cand=t; break
    if cand is None:
        print("cycle",remaining); break
    merged.append(cand); remaining.remove(cand)
print(merged)
print(classmap)
print("regular order excluding specials:")
specials=["Background","PreWrapper","Error","LineLink","LineTableTD","LineTable","LineHighlight","LineNumbersTable","LineNumbers","Line"]
print([x for x in merged if x not in specials])
PY
python3 /tmp/gen_token_order.py

    R(r"[\s\S]+?(?=<\?|\Z)", U("html")),
]}
GO_HTML_RULES = {"root": [
    R(r"{{-?.*?-?}}", U("go-template")),
    R(r"[\s\S]+?(?={{|\Z)", U("html")),
]}
SVELTE_RULES = {"root": [

    R(r"[\s\S]+?(?={|\Z)", U("html")),
]}

    "go": GO_RULES,
    "http": HTTP_RULES,
    "rst": RST_RULES,
    "raku": RAKU_RULES,
    "haxe": HAXE_RULES,

def tokenise_custom(tokeniser, lexer, text, sub=False):
    key = lexer.custom
    if key in ("common_lisp", "emacs_lisp"):
        states = _lisp_rules(CL_KEYWORDS, CL_BUILTINS)
    elif key in CUSTOM_STATES:
        states = CUSTOM_STATES[key]
    else:
        return [("Text", text)] if text else []
    ckey = (key, lexer.name)
    sub_lexer = _cache.get(ckey)
    if sub_lexer is None:
        data = dict(lexer.data)
        data["states"] = states
        data["custom"] = None
        sub_lexer = Lexer(data)
        sub_lexer.name = lexer.name
        sub_lexer.registry = lexer.registry
        _cache[ckey] = sub_lexer
    return tokeniser._tokenise_regex(sub_lexer, text, "root")

p='src/lexer_engine.py'; s=open(p).read()
patch = r'''
def _fix_first_negated_category(pat):
    # The reference regex engine (regexp2) has a quirk: when a character
    # class begins with a negated shorthand (\W, \D or \S), shorthand
    # category tokens immediately following it are ignored.  E.g.
    # [^\W\d] behaves as [^\W] (i.e. \w), not as [^\W\d] does in Python.
    out = []
    i = 0
    n = len(pat)
    while i < n:
        c = pat[i]
        if c == '\\' and i + 1 < n:
            out.append(pat[i:i+2]); i += 2; continue
        if c != '[':
            out.append(c); i += 1; continue
        # parse a character class
        j = i + 1
        neg = False
        if j < n and pat[j] == '^':
            neg = True; j += 1
        first = j
        # a ']' as first char is a literal
        k = j
        if k < n and pat[k] == ']':
            k += 1
        while k < n:
            if pat[k] == '\\' and k + 1 < n:
                k += 2; continue
            if pat[k] == ']':
                break
            k += 1
        if k >= n:
            out.append(pat[i:]); break
        content_start = first
        # check first element
        modified = pat[i:k+1]
        if pat[first:first+2] in (r'\W', r'\D', r'\S'):
            # drop contiguous shorthand category tokens after the first
            p2 = first + 2
            kept_tail_start = p2
            while p2 + 1 < k and pat[p2] == '\\' and pat[p2+1] in 'wWdDsS':
                p2 += 2
            if p2 > kept_tail_start:
                modified = pat[i:first+2] + pat[p2:k+1]
        out.append(modified)
        i = k + 1
    return ''.join(out)

'''
s=s.replace("# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Regex translation", "# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Regex translation")
# insert before _translate_pattern definition
s=s.replace("def _translate_pattern(pat):", patch + "def _translate_pattern(pat):")
# call it at start of _translate_pattern: add line after its comment block start
s=s.replace("    # Handle \\p{...} / \\pX, \\x{...}, \\u{...}, possessive quantifiers,\n    # atomic groups, keeping track of character classes.\n    out = []",
              "    # Handle \\p{...} / \\pX, \\x{...}, \\u{...}, possessive quantifiers,\n    # atomic groups, keeping track of character classes.\n    pat = _fix_first_negated_category(pat)\n    out = []")
open(p,'w').write(s)

import subprocess, os, json, re
REF="/tmp/reference_executable"; OUR="/workspace/executable"
fails=[]; total=0
def cmp(args, inp=None, cwd=None, label=None, norm_trace=False):
    global total; total+=1
    try: r=subprocess.run([REF]+args,input=inp,capture_output=True,timeout=6,cwd=cwd)
    except Exception as e: print("REF timeout",args); return
    try: o=subprocess.run([OUR]+args,input=inp,capture_output=True,timeout=6,cwd=cwd)
    except Exception as e: print("OUR timeout",args,e); fails.append(args); return
    def norm(b):
        b=b.replace(b"reference_executable",b"executable")
        if norm_trace:
            b=re.sub(rb'"elapsedMs":[0-9.eE+-]+',b'"elapsedMs":0',b)
        return b
    if r.returncode!=o.returncode or norm(r.stdout)!=o.stdout or norm(r.stderr)!=o.stderr:
        fails.append(args)
        print(f"\n=== DIFF {label or args} inp={inp!r:.80} cwd={cwd}")
        print(" rc",r.returncode,o.returncode)
        if norm(r.stdout)!=o.stdout: print(" refout",norm(r.stdout)[:1200]); print(" ourout",o.stdout[:1200])
        if norm(r.stderr)!=o.stderr: print(" referr",norm(r.stderr)[:1000]); print(" ourerr",o.stderr[:1000])

# all lexers from index, generic sample and alphabet soup
index=json.load(open("src/data/lexers_index.json"))
soup=b"foo bar 123 0xFF 1.5 'str' \"dq\" <tag attr=1> {a: [1,2]} //c #c ;c\ndef x(a+b): return a->b $var @decorator |pipe| & [[x]]\n"
for ent in index:
    alias = (ent.get("aliases") or [ent["name"]])[0]
    cmp(["-s","monokai","-l",alias,"-f","tokens"], inp=soup, label=f"lexer {ent['name']}/{alias}")
print(f"after lexers TOTAL {total} fails {len(fails)}")
# all styles for a sample
code=b"def foo(x):\n    s = 'hi' + str(x)  # c\n    return s\n"
styles=[]
for line in open("src/data/list.txt"):
    if line.startswith("styles:"): styles=line.split(":",1)[1].split()
for st in styles:
    for fmt in ["terminal","terminal16","terminal256","terminal16m"]:
        cmp(["-s",st,"-l","python","-f",fmt], inp=code, label=f"style {st}/{fmt}")
    cmp(["-s",st,"-l","python","--html","--html-only"], inp=code, label=f"style {st}/html")
    cmp(["-s",st,"-l","python","--html","--html-only","--html-inline-styles"], inp=code, label=f"style {st}/inline")
print(f"after styles TOTAL {total} fails {len(fails)}")
# autodetect / filename
os.makedirs("/tmp/dt",exist_ok=True)
files={
 "a.py":b"x = 1\n", "a.go":b"package main\n", "a.unknown":b"hello\n", "noext":b"#!/bin/bash\necho hi\n",
 "b.txt":b"plain text\n", "Makefile":b"all:\n\techo hi\n", "empty.py":b"", "empty":b"",
 "script":b"package main\n", "data":b"#include <stdio.h>\nint main(){}\n", "x.json":b'{"a":1}\n'
}
for fn,data in files.items(): open(f"/tmp/dt/{fn}","wb").write(data)
for fn in files:
    for extra in [[],["--fail"],["-f","tokens"],["-f","tokens","--fail"],["--check"],["--unbuffered","--fail"]]:
        cmp(["-s","monokai"]+extra+[f"/tmp/dt/{fn}"], inp=None, label=f"file {fn} {extra}")
for fn,inp in [("x.py",b"x=1\n"),("x.go",b"x\n"),("Makefile",b"all:\n"),("x.unknown",b"#!/bin/bash\necho\n"),("",b"#!/bin/sh\necho\n"),("python",b"x\n")]:
    cmp(["-s","monokai","-f","tokens",f"--filename={fn}"], inp=inp, label=f"filename {fn}")
for inp in [b"",b"x\n",b"#!/bin/bash\necho\n",b"#include <vector>\nusing namespace std;\n",b"func _ready():\n",b"package main\nfunc foo()\n",b"**free\n",b"hello\n"]:
    cmp(["-s","monokai","-f","tokens"], inp=inp, label="autodetect stdin")
    cmp(["-s","monokai","--fail","-f","tokens"], inp=inp, label="autodetect fail")
# multiple files / dir / missing etc
cmp(["-s","monokai","/tmp/dt/a.py","/tmp/dt/a.go"], inp=None)
cmp(["-s","monokai","--check","/tmp/dt/a.py"], inp=None)
open("/tmp/dt/err.py","wb").write(b"x = ` \ny=`\n")
cmp(["-s","monokai","--check","/tmp/dt/err.py"], inp=None)
cmp(["-s","monokai","--check","err.py"], inp=None, cwd="/tmp/dt")
cmp(["-s","monokai","--check"], inp=b"`\n")
cmp(["-s","monokai","-l","python","--trace","-f","tokens"], inp=b"x=1\n", norm_trace=True, label="trace python")
cmp(["-s","monokai","-l","c","--trace","-f","tokens"], inp=b"int main(){}\n", norm_trace=True, label="trace c")
cmp(["-s","monokai","--trace","-f","tokens"], inp=b"hello\n", norm_trace=True, label="trace fallback")
print(f"\nTOTAL {total} fails {len(fails)}")
PY

import subprocess, os, glob, shutil, filecmp
REF="/tmp/reference_executable"; OUR="/workspace/executable"
fails=[]; total=0
def cmp(args, inp=None, cwd=None, label=None):
    global total; total+=1
    try: r=subprocess.run([REF]+args,input=inp,capture_output=True,timeout=6,cwd=cwd)
    except Exception as e: print("REF timeout",args); return
    try: o=subprocess.run([OUR]+args,input=inp,capture_output=True,timeout=6,cwd=cwd)
    except Exception as e: print("OUR timeout",args,e); fails.append(args); return
    def norm(b): return b.replace(b"reference_executable",b"executable")
    if r.returncode!=o.returncode or norm(r.stdout)!=o.stdout or norm(r.stderr)!=o.stderr:
        fails.append(args)
        print(f"\n=== DIFF {label or args} cwd={cwd}")
        print(" rc",r.returncode,o.returncode)
        if norm(r.stdout)!=o.stdout: print(" refout",norm(r.stdout)[:1200]); print(" ourout",o.stdout[:1200])
        if norm(r.stderr)!=o.stderr: print(" referr",norm(r.stderr)[:1000]); print(" ourerr",o.stderr[:1000])

os.makedirs("/tmp/cust/sub",exist_ok=True)
lexxml='''<lexer><config><name>MyLex</name><alias>mylex</alias><filename>*.mine</filename></config>
<rules><state name="root">
<rule pattern="(foo)([0-9]+)"><bygroups><token type="Keyword"/><token type="LiteralNumberInteger"/></bygroups></rule>
<rule pattern="bar"><token type="NameFunction"/><push state="inner"/></rule>
<rule pattern="\\s+"><token type="Text"/></rule>
<rule pattern="."><token type="Text"/></rule>
</state><state name="inner"><rule pattern="x"><token type="Operator"/><pop depth="1"/></rule><rule pattern="."><token type="Name"/></rule></state></rules></lexer>'''
for name in ["mylex.custom","mylex.xml","sub/other.custom"]:
    open(f"/tmp/cust/{name}","w").write(lexxml)
open("/tmp/cust/bad.custom","w").write("not xml")
open("/tmp/cust/badtype.custom","w").write('<lexer><config><name>Bad</name></config><rules><state name="root"><rule pattern="a"><token type="Nope"/></rule></state></rules></lexer>')
open("/tmp/cust/badgroups.custom","w").write('<lexer><config><name>Bad</name></config><rules><state name="root"><rule pattern="(a)(b)(c)"><bygroups><token type="Keyword"/></bygroups></rule></state></rules></lexer>')
open("/tmp/cust/badregex.custom","w").write('<lexer><config><name>Bad</name></config><rules><state name="root"><rule pattern="("><token type="Keyword"/></rule></state></rules></lexer>')
open("/tmp/cust/badinclude.custom","w").write('<lexer><config><name>Bad</name></config><rules><state name="root"><rule><include state="nosuch"/></rule></state></rules></lexer>')
for name in ["mylex.custom","mylex.xml","sub/other.custom","./mylex.custom","bad.custom","badtype.custom","badgroups.custom","badregex.custom","badinclude.custom","nonexistent.custom","sub",".",".."]:
    for fmt in ["tokens","terminal"]:
        cmp(["-s","monokai","-l",name,"-f",fmt], inp=b"foo42 barxy foo\n", cwd="/tmp/cust", label=f"custlex {name}")
    cmp(["-s","monokai","-l",f"/tmp/cust/{name}","-f","tokens"], inp=b"foo42\n", cwd="/tmp/cust", label=f"custlex abs {name}")
    cmp(["-s","monokai","-l",f"/tmp/cust/{name}","-f","tokens"], inp=b"foo42\n", cwd="/workspace", label=f"custlex abs from ws {name}")

# custom styles
styles={
 "s1.xml":'<style name="test"><entry type="Background" style="#ffffff bg:#000000"/><entry type="Keyword" style="#ff0000 bold"/><entry type="LiteralString" style="#00ff00 italic bg:#111111"/></style>',
 "s2.xml":'<style name="test2"><entry type="Text" style="#123456 italic"/><entry type="Keyword" style="bold"/></style>',
 "empty.xml":"", "bad.xml":"<foo/>", "badtype.xml":'<style name="x"><entry type="Nope" style="#fff"/></style>',
 "badstyle.xml":'<style name="x"><entry type="Keyword" style="zzz"/></style>',
 "text.txt":"hello", "unclosed.xml":'<style name="x">',
}
for fn,content in styles.items(): open(f"/tmp/cust/{fn}","w").write(content)
for fn in styles:
    for extra in [["--html-styles"],["-l","python","-f","terminal16m"],["-l","python","--html","--html-only"],["-l","python","--html","--html-only","--html-inline-styles"]]:
        cmp(["-s",f"/tmp/cust/{fn}"]+extra, inp=b"if x: 's'\n", label=f"style {fn} {extra}")
for name in ["swapoff","SWAPOFF","nosuchstyle"]:
    cmp(["-s",name,"-l","python"], inp=b"x\n", cwd="/tmp/cust")
# file named swapoff in cust dir
open("/tmp/cust/swapoff","w").write(styles["s1.xml"])
cmp([], inp=b"if x\n", cwd="/tmp/cust", label="default style swapoff file present")

# XML dump into separate dirs, compare filenames and canonicalised contents (sort state blocks? just compare sorted file bytes list may differ due state order - report separately)
for d in ["/tmp/xml_ref","/tmp/xml_our"]:
    shutil.rmtree(d,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(d)
r=subprocess.run([REF,"--xml=/tmp/xml_ref"],capture_output=True,timeout=10)
o=subprocess.run([OUR,"--xml=/tmp/xml_our"],capture_output=True,timeout=10)
print("xml rc",r.returncode,o.returncode,"stderr same-ish",r.stderr[:300],o.stderr[:300])
rf=sorted(os.listdir("/tmp/xml_ref")); of=sorted(os.listdir("/tmp/xml_our"))
print("xml files same names", rf==of, len(rf), len(of))
if rf!=of: print(" only ref",set(rf)-set(of),"only our",set(of)-set(rf))
diff_files=[]
for fn in rf:
    if fn in of and open(f"/tmp/xml_ref/{fn}","rb").read()!=open(f"/tmp/xml_our/{fn}","rb").read(): diff_files.append(fn)
print("xml content diff count",len(diff_files),diff_files[:20])
total+=1
# second dump over existing files (warnings)
r=subprocess.run([REF,"--xml=/tmp/xml_ref"],capture_output=True,timeout=10)
o=subprocess.run([OUR,"--xml=/tmp/xml_our"],capture_output=True,timeout=10)
# normalize dir names
def nz(b): return b.replace(b"xml_ref",b"xml_X").replace(b"xml_our",b"xml_X").replace(b"reference_executable",b"executable")
print("xml second rc",r.returncode,o.returncode,"stderr equal after dir norm",nz(r.stderr)==nz(o.stderr))
if nz(r.stderr)!=nz(o.stderr):
    print(nz(r.stderr)[:1000]); print(nz(o.stderr)[:1000])
print(f"\nTOTAL {total} fails {len(fails)}")
PY

cat > /tmp/difftest6.py << 'PY'
import subprocess, glob
REF="/tmp/reference_executable"; OUR="/workspace/executable"
fails=0; total=0
def cmp(args,label):
    global fails,total; total+=1
    r=subprocess.run([REF]+args,capture_output=True,timeout=15)
    o=subprocess.run([OUR]+args,capture_output=True,timeout=15)
    def n(b):return b.replace(b"reference_executable",b"executable")
    if r.returncode!=o.returncode or n(r.stdout)!=o.stdout or n(r.stderr)!=o.stderr:
        fails+=1; print("DIFF",label,"rc",r.returncode,o.returncode,"lens",len(r.stdout),len(o.stdout))
        a=n(r.stdout); b=o.stdout; i=next((i for i in range(min(len(a),len(b))) if a[i]!=b[i]),min(len(a),len(b)))
        print(" at",i,"ref",a[max(0,i-200):i+300]); print(" our",b[max(0,i-200):i+300])
        if n(r.stderr)!=o.stderr: print("err",n(r.stderr)[:500],o.stderr[:500])
files=glob.glob("src/*.py")+["README.md","compile.sh"]
for f in files:
    for fmt in ["tokens","terminal","terminal256"]:
        cmp(["-s","monokai","-f",fmt,f],f"{f}/{fmt}")
    cmp(["-s","github","--html","--html-only",f],f"{f}/html")
    cmp(["-s","monokai","--check",f],f"{f}/check")
# XML lexer/style data as XML file input
for f in sorted(glob.glob("/tmp/xmlout/*.xml"))[:20]:
    cmp(["-s","monokai","-l","xml","-f","tokens",f],f"xmlfile {f}")
print("TOTAL",total,"fails",fails)
PY

    r=subprocess.run([REF]+args,input=inp,capture_output=True,timeout=8)

    def n(b):return b.replace(b"reference_executable",b"executable")
